title: United 232: functional redundancy is not physical independence
focus: Test redundant architecture against shared physical hazards and the operational capability remaining after damage.

sources.title: FAA Lessons Learned: United Airlines Flight 232, N1819U
sources.limitations: The FAA account was inspected. The original NTSB report URL was unavailable during curation; this case does not represent direct access to that report.

facts.statement: The FAA describes an uncontained tail-engine fan-disk failure whose debris damaged all three hydraulic systems.
The systems were functionally isolated but physically close in parts of the tail; the crew used wing-engine thrust to obtain limited control.

retrospective.boundary: Engines, debris zones, hydraulic routing, flight controls, crew coordination, airport options, and emergency response define the damaged-aircraft system.
interfaces: Engine debris → multiple channels: a single event can cross logical redundancy boundaries.
Remaining propulsion → crew control: residual authority may be difficult to use and insufficient for stable flight.

decision.question: How should a redundancy claim be challenged?
options: Trace shared locations, supplies, controls, maintenance, and external hazards.
decision.recommendation: Pair functional decomposition with a physical dependency review and degraded-operation evidence.
decision.uncertainty: Physical separation is one design choice; effectiveness depends on the hazard envelope and achievable residual control.

rows: State achievable tasks after shared damage
Assign navigation, control, communication, and cabin coordination

questions: Which diagram would reveal a weakness hidden by a logical block diagram?
What is the difference between having some control and meeting a landing requirement?
Write a qualified redundancy claim for a new design.
answer_signals: Identifies shared hazard exposure instead of multiplying nominal reliabilities.
Defines residual capability in operational tasks.
Recognizes human adaptation without turning it into a guaranteed design control.
retrospective.transfer_exercise: Synthetic: three power channels share a service duct. Produce a common-cause review and compare relocation, shielding, and diverse backup.
retrospective.limits: No reliability probability, debris simulation, or claim that training alone would resolve the failure is made.
